newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve stricter worker protection rules.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve stricter worker protection rules.

text.p: The European Parliament on Wednesday approved with amendments a draft European Union directive designed to protect workers from the risks associated with exposure to carcinogens.
Draft directive COM(95)425 extends the scope of an existing directive on worker protection dating from 1990.
It covers the handling and preparation of substances not covered by the existing law and sets for the first time a limit on the use of benzene.
In a report drafted by Finnish Nordic Left Euro-MP Outi Ojala, parliament said the proposal would improve health and safety protection for workers.
But Euro-MPs voiced disappointment that EU ministers had not taken on board the amendments to the text parliament had requested at first reading last June.

They were particularly annoyed that the Council of Ministers had extended the transition period for introducing the new rules and had not included arsenic and its compounds on the list of additional substances for which the EU urgently must set limit values.

They reintroduced their amendments, even though European Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn told them before the vote the European Commission sympathised with their demands but could not accept them because there was insufficient technical data to back them up.
The draft directive must have the approval of both the Council and the parliament to become law.
